1200.author: yuanzhou75
1200.body:
Closes #1152

Stage 2 of the issue: the pipeline no longer materialises an archive on either side, the default cap moves to 5 GiB, and both sides check the machine before starting rather than failing halfway.

## What changed

**Export.** `writeResearchPackage` writes tar → gzip → the task's own file; the background export hands it a destination, so there is no whole-archive buffer, and a cancelled or failed task deletes a partial file instead of discarding one. Objects are handed over as sources — a CAS stream, or a workspace file read twice — so the payload is not all resident.

**Import.** `importResearchPackageStreamed` takes the compressed bytes as they arrive, gunzips incrementally, parses the tar sequentially and writes each object to `objectDirectory/<sha256>` while hashing it, so a digest is verified against its address before the object can be used. Manifest, records and readme are the only resident entries; the object map is backed by that directory and reads one object at a time.

**HTTP.** `POST .../research-package/inspect` and `.../import` stream the upload to `<data dir>/research-package-uploads/<purpose>-XXXX/package.sdresearch` and parse it from there. The inspection cache now owns that directory instead of a `Buffer`; a cached import deletes it only after the restore has copied the archive into its snapshot, and a read-only restore uses `copyFile(..., COPYFILE_EXCL)` instead of rewriting bytes.

**Preflight.** Each side is charged only what it writes: an export against the preview's `archiveBytes` (one compressed file, the uncompressed estimate being an upper bound); an upload against `content-length` (the staged file); a streamed parse against `min(ceiling, free disk / 3)`, which reserves the two copies a later restore adds; a restore against `2 × unpacked + records` on disk (snapshot objects and CAS blobs — the unpacked upload is already there) and `max(largest object, records) + 256 MiB` in memory. `inspect` charges nothing after its parse, because it writes nothing more. Memory is measured on `MemAvailable` so reclaimable page cache counts. Insufficient capacity is refused with HTTP 507 and `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK` / `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY`, naming what is missing.

**Cap.** Default 5 GiB, ceiling `8 GiB - 1` — the largest value an 11-digit octal tar header field can express, so the existing header writer stays valid; a single entry beyond it is refused instead of producing a broken header. The upload bound stays derived from the ceiling, as #1173 left it.

## Measurements

Incompressible payload, one object, this host (Windows, 15.7 GiB RAM), `--max-old-space-size=3072`, one process per mode, `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` after each step:

| payload | archive | export peak — before (whole archive) | export peak — streaming | import peak — before | import peak — streaming |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 256 MiB | 256.1 MiB | 1082 MiB | 141 MiB | 1164 MiB | 152 MiB |
| 300 MiB | 300.1 MiB | 1260 MiB | 139 MiB | 1300 MiB | 145 MiB |
| 500 MiB | 500.2 MiB | 2066 MiB | 139 MiB | 2101 MiB | 179 MiB |
| 5100 MiB (5 GiB class) | 5101.6 MiB | not run — needs ~15 GiB resident | 155 MiB | not run | 459 MiB |

The "before" column reproduces the numbers the issue measured (1071 / 1248 / 2056 MiB at 256 / 300 / 500 MiB). Times on the same runs, 256 / 300 / 500 MiB: export 11 / 15.6 / 29.4 s before and 10.6 / 15.2 / 28.5 s streaming; import 0.9 / 1.1 / 3.0 s before and 1.9 / 4.9 / 6.2 s streaming — the streamed import writes each object to disk and copies it. The 5 GiB-class round trip exported in 269 s and imported in 81 s at 155 MiB / 459 MiB peak, on a host whose `--max-old-space-size` is the API default.

## Tests

- `packages/research-package/src/index.test.ts` 16/16 and `stream-import.test.ts` 4/4: the streamed import matches the in-memory import on records, inventory and package checksum; a flipped payload byte fails the per-object digest check; a truncated archive and an over-cap archive are refused.
- `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` 23/23, `research-package-exports.test.ts` 9/9 (including a failed streamed write leaving no partial archive), `conversation-branches.test.ts` 6/6, `research-package-overcap-roundtrip.test.ts` 1/1, `research-package-preflight.test.ts` 5/5.
- The tagged suites were run on this host with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run and restored before pushing; the tags in this commit are unchanged.
- Mutations: dropping the per-object digest check fails the tampered-payload case; removing the preflight refusal fails both refusal cases; removing the partial-file cleanup fails the write-failure case.
- `tsc -p services/api`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` and the package build are clean.

## Limits worth knowing

- A workspace file is read three times: once to name the object, once by the writer's hash pass, once by the tar pass. A CAS object is read twice. Turning the hash pass off would need the caller's checksum to be trusted; this PR does not trust it.
- The streamed import is slower per byte than the buffered one (see the times above) because each object is written to disk and then copied; that is the trade for bounded memory.
- Old packages are unaffected: the format is unchanged and an import still accepts the hard ceiling.
- No user-visible copy changed in this PR: the stage-1 limit line and over-cap confirmation are #1173, already merged. The two preflight refusals surface through the existing task error, with their message naming the missing capacity.
- The measurements above are of the package library round trip. The API restore reads one object at a time rather than materialising the package; its footprint is the largest single object plus records, which the post-parse preflight enforces.

A refusal caused by the measured free-disk budget answers HTTP 507 with `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK` and the disk copy; an overrun of the absolute ceiling stays its own client-input error.
1200.head: fix-1152-streaming-package
1200.title: feat(research-package): stream both sides of a package and raise the cap to 5 GiB

1206.author: yuanzhou75
1206.body:
Closes #1204

## What changes

**The composer shows the permission mode and lets it be changed there.** The mode existed only behind the composer's settings menu, so what the next turn would run under was invisible until that menu was opened; the composer footer now carries a compact selector after the + and settings buttons:

- closed, it is the shield plus the mode's own word — `请求批准` with a check mark, `完全访问` with an exclamation mark and in the warning colour the flyout row already uses;
- when nothing has been chosen yet and no session detail is loaded, it says `跟随设置` / "Follow settings" instead of claiming `请求批准`: the service applies the project or global `defaultApprovalMode`, which can be full access, so the unset state must not name a policy (#1206 review);
- open, it is the same two-row scope flyout the settings menu shows, so the scope descriptions live in one place rather than being copied;
- it is disabled while a run is active, for the same reason the settings row is;
- the settings row keeps its choice: this adds a visible door, it does not remove the existing one.

**A new conversation starts in the last mode the reader selected, and that survives a restart.** `apps/desktop/src/app/approval-mode-preference.ts` keeps the choice in desktop storage under a namespaced key (`sciencediscovery-desktop:approval-mode`), next to the panel-width and locale preferences. It is read on creation, and a stored value that is not one of the two modes is treated as no choice at all. Consequences:

- conversations that already exist are never updated by it — nothing here writes to them, and reopening one only displays its own mode;
- the choice travels only in creation-time values: `CreateSessionRequest.approvalMode` for the normal path, and one `updateSession(approvalMode)` for the project-creation path, whose first conversation the service creates with its own default;
- with nothing stored, the request carries no `approvalMode` and the service default applies exactly as before.

No API change was needed: `CreateSessionRequest` already accepts `approvalMode` and the server route honours it. Permission enforcement is untouched.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop/tests/approval-mode-preference.test.ts`: 3 cases — a fresh call after `rememberApprovalMode` carries the mode (this is what a restart looks like, because the module keeps no state of its own); a stored value that is not a mode is ignored; `inheritForSession` applies the remembered mode to a conversation created by another path and makes no request when nothing is remembered.
- `apps/desktop/tests/composer.test.tsx`: 31 cases, four covering this change — the selector's position after the + and settings buttons with the asking label and check, the full-access warning colour and label, the unset `跟随设置` state (neither colour), and the popover's two scope explanations with the callback receiving `ask_for_dangerous` when that row is chosen.
- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and the root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean. `pnpm ci:l1` and the rest of the gate are CI's evidence.

## Verification of the restart requirement

This was the one acceptance criterion the first head missed, so it is stated explicitly: the choice is written to `localStorage` on every selection (`sciencediscovery-desktop:approval-mode`), and the capture run below read it back after selecting full access (`stored: "always_allow"`). A fresh module instance reads it through `readStoredText`, which is what a new application process does; the unit test uses a storage stub to exercise exactly that read.

## Screenshots

| state | en | zh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before (composer, no selector) | ![before, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-before.png) | ![before, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-before.png) |
| unset, 跟随设置 | ![unset, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-unset.png) | ![unset, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-unset.png) |
| closed, 请求批准 (shield + check) | ![ask, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-ask.png) | ![ask, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-ask.png) |
| closed, 完全访问 (warning colour) | ![full, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-full.png) | ![full, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-full.png) |
| open flyout, both scope explanations | ![flyout, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-flyout.png) | ![flyout, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-flyout.png) |

Captured from the running desktop shell (vite dev + the repository's `e2e/fixtures` control plane), zh and en, 1440×900, on this head. The text was checked programmatically, not by eye: the DOM read back `跟随设置` / `请求批准` / `完全访问` and both scope explanations exactly, so the Chinese in these captures is the dictionary's own string rather than a re-encoded one — the #1148 failure was a transcoding bug and there is none here. The capture script also asserted the classes (`is-unset`, `is-danger`) and that selecting full access stored `always_allow`.
1206.head: fix-1204-composer-permission-selector
1206.title: feat(desktop): show the permission mode in the composer and inherit it for new conversations

1207.author: yuanzhou75
1207.body:
Closes #1205

A conversation created after the user has picked a model now starts from that model, within the same running instance. Only the picker's explicit choice writes the memory: opening an existing conversation reads its own model and must not become the default for the next one. Restart persistence stays out of scope — that is #1204.

## What changed

- **`session-model-memory.ts`**: one decision, `modelForNewConversation(remembered, models)`. It returns the remembered id only while this instance's catalog still carries it, so a retired model is never handed to the server and the picker shows the real fallback instead of a dangling selection.
- **`use-workspace.ts`**:
  - the picker records the model as soon as the user picks it, before the session write, so a conversation created while that write is still in flight already starts from the new choice;
  - `createOpenSession` sends `modelId` when the remembered model is available, instead of leaving the server to apply the project/global default;
  - a fresh draft shows the remembered model (falling back to the project default, then the global default, then the first catalog model);
  - a new Project's untitled conversation is switched to the remembered model with the ordinary session update, and a failure there is not fatal — opening the conversation reads its real model;
  - a catalog refresh that no longer carries the remembered model clears it, so nothing dangles.

## Behaviour, against the acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How it holds |
| --- | --- |
| A new conversation defaults to the last explicitly selected model | `createOpenSession` sends it; the draft's picker shows it |
| A later selection is used by subsequently created conversations | the picker writes the memory on every explicit choice |
| Conversations with messages keep their own model; reopening does not change the memory | `openSession` only clears the one-shot draft override and shows that conversation's `modelId`; it never writes the remembered value |
| An unavailable remembered model does not leave a dangling selection | `modelForNewConversation` returns nothing for an id the catalog lost, and the refresh clears the memory; the project/global default applies |
| Relevant automated tests | `session-model-memory.test.ts` covers the three decision cases; the existing `workspace-model-setup.test.ts` still passes, including "new drafts automatically select a model while preserving project and explicit choices" |

## Verification

- `apps/desktop/tests/session-model-memory.test.ts` **3/3** and `apps/desktop/tests/workspace-model-setup.test.ts` **3/3**, run on this host with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run and restored — the tags in this commit are unchanged.
- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are clean.
- No user-visible copy changed, so the localization files are untouched.

## What this PR does not claim

- I did not get a hook-level test for the creation path running on this host: mounting `useWorkspace` against a fake client enters the desktop boot path that also asks for `/api/health` and `POST /api/inbox`, and the harness I wrote for it did not settle, so I did not ship a test that cannot run. The decision itself is unit-tested and the creation path is a single call to it; if a reviewer wants the hook case too, the honest way is to extend the existing boot harness rather than bolt a second fake onto it, and I will do that on request.
- Restart persistence is deliberately absent (#1204 owns it); the memory lives for the instance.
- The web client is unchanged: this request pairs with #1204's desktop composer work, and the web client's new-conversation model continues to follow its server/project default.
1207.head: fix-1205-model-memory
1207.title: feat(desktop): start a new conversation from the model last picked

1208.author: yuanzhou75
1208.body:
Follow-up to #1194 (#1182 and #1187 both closed by it): the three suggestions that were deliberately not pushed onto the approved head.

## What changes

**F1 — the read-only fixture is judged by its own write (`application/test/bootstrap.test.ts`).**
`hostMadeReadOnly` had its `writeFile` and its conditional `rm` inside one `try`, so a failed unlink of a file the host had just created was classified as "read-only". Only the write decides now; the unlink is best effort. It failed loudly rather than passing silently, but the classification was wrong.

**F3 — the writable half runs before the skip (same file).**
`assert.equal(await dirWritable(join(root, "rw")), true)` had moved below the NTFS probe, so on the one platform this suite runs on, a regression that made `dirWritable` answer `false` for a writable directory would have been reported as `# skipped`. It is asserted before the probe again, and only the read-only assertion sits below the skip.

**F2 — the build-only flag is pinned in the contract (`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`).**
`/pnpm --dir application dist/` matches with or without `--publish never`, so the publish half of the Windows gate had no contract check while the split half did. The contract now asserts the flag, so a later edit cannot restore electron-builder's implicit publish (the #1187 failure) while the test stays green.

## Validation

On this Windows 11 host (Node v22.23.4), against the exact files pushed:

- `application/test/bootstrap.test.ts`: **34 tests, 32 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped** — the same two NTFS skips, with the writable assertion now before the probe.
- `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: `Windows distribution gate builds the native Electron installer` passes, including the new `--publish never` assertion (run with that file's `os:linux` tag released for this host; the other failures in the file are unrelated absolute-path assertions that assume Linux and are untouched here).
- Root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` is clean for these files through CI's gate.

This is test-only; no product or workflow behaviour changes.
1208.head: fix-1194-review-followups
1208.title: test(application): close the three review suggestions deferred from #1194
